title_ar: الشيخ الددو ما يحدث في مصر هو جريمة فادحة ينكرها الشرع الحنيف
title_en: Sheikh al-Dedew: What Is Happening in Egypt Is a Grievous Crime That the Upright Sharia Condemns
body_ar:
أصدر فضيلة الشيخ محمد الحسن ولد الددو اليوم الأربعاء 7 شوال 1434هـ الموافق 14 أغشت 2013م فتوى بشأن تطور وتسارع الأحداث في مصر مؤكدا أن ما يحدث في مصر هو مؤامرة كبيرة يتعرض لها شعب مصر العظيم دبرها أعداء الإسلام من الداخل والخارج وتولى تنفيذها وزير الدفاع الفريق عبد الفتاح السيسي وأعوانه..

واستنكر الشيخ الددو في الفتوى بشدة ما حدث اليوم من جرائم نتيجة اقتحام الميادين في مصر وقتل المعتصمين السلميين؛ والذين من بينهم عشرات العلماء الأزهريين في أكبر جريمة عرفتها مصر في تاريخها الإسلامي.

وأكد فضيلة الشيخ أن من واجب علماء الأمة أن يبينوا الموقف الشرعي الذي لا غبار عليه مما يجري في مصر.

وبَيَّن الشيخ أن قتل المسلمين بغير حق من أكبر ما يقع على وجه الأرض من الجرائم، مضيفا أن العبث بأمن مصر ومقدراتها وإرادة شعبها العظيم هو جريمة فادحة ينكرها الشرع الحنيف.

مؤكدا أن من قُتل في هذه الاعتصامات أو المسيرات من المسلمين المسالمين الصادقين شهداء في سبيل الله، فقد قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم: "من قتل دون ماله فهو شهيد" متفق عليه.

وختم فضيلة الشيخ الفتوى بتسجيل الاعتراض والدهشة من مسلك بعض الدول التي بادرت بالاعتراف بالانقلاب، وهذا يقول الشيخ من التعاون على الإثم والعدوان.

وقد وَقَّع الفتوى إضافة إلى الشيخ الددو فضيلة الشيخ محمد عبد الرحمن ولد أحمد الملقب ولد فتى.

لتحميل الفتوى اضغط هنا

مضمون الفتوى اضغط هنا
body_en:
His Eminence Sheikh Muhammad al-Hasan Ould al-Dedew issued today, Wednesday 7 Shawwal 1434 AH, corresponding to 14 August 2013, a considered legal opinion (fatwā) concerning the development and acceleration of events in Egypt, affirming that what is happening in Egypt is a great conspiracy to which the great people of Egypt are being subjected, contrived by the enemies of Islam within and without, and whose execution has been undertaken by the minister of defence, General Abdel Fattah el-Sisi, and his helpers…

In the fatwā Sheikh al-Dedew condemned in the strongest terms the crimes that took place today as a result of the storming of the squares in Egypt and the killing of the peaceful sit-in participants — among whom were dozens of Azhari scholars — in the greatest crime Egypt has known in its Islamic history.

His Eminence the Sheikh affirmed that it is the duty of the community's scholars to set out the position of the Sharia, beyond any question, on what is taking place in Egypt.

The Sheikh made clear that the killing of Muslims without right is among the greatest crimes that occur on the face of the earth, adding that the tampering with the security of Egypt, with its resources and with the will of its great people is a grievous crime that the upright Sharia condemns.

He affirmed that those killed in these sit-ins or marches, from among the peaceable and sincere Muslims, are martyrs on God's path — for the Messenger of God (peace and blessings be upon him) said: 'Whoever is killed defending his property is a martyr' (agreed upon).

His Eminence the Sheikh closed the fatwā by recording his objection to, and astonishment at, the course taken by some states that hastened to recognise the coup; and this, the Sheikh says, is part of cooperating in sin and transgression.

The fatwā was signed, in addition to Sheikh al-Dedew, by His Eminence Shaykh Muhammad Abd al-Rahman Ould Ahmad, known as Ould Fata.

flags.note: EDITORIAL REVIEW — high exposure. The text names the present president of Egypt by name and rank as the executor of a conspiracy against Islam, calls the events of 14 August 2013 a coup, and rules that states recognising it are cooperating in sin and transgression (an echo of Sūrat al-Māʾidah 5:2). Egypt's defamation and 'insulting state institutions' provisions make this material dangerous to republish in some jurisdictions. Translated faithfully — neither softened nor strengthened — and the decision on publication belongs to Ummah Collective and the Sheikh's office.

flags.arabic: "من قتل دون ماله فهو شهيد" متفق عليه
flags.context: the report cited in support of the claim that those killed are martyrs
options: translate as printed, with the grading as given
note that the wording cited concerns property, not the claim being made
flags.note: The report is cited as 'agreed upon' (al-Bukhari and Muslim) and that attribution is reproduced exactly, with no grading added or removed (style guide §4). Note for the reviewer only, and not a correction: the wording quoted here is the 'دون ماله' (defending his property) form, whereas the claim being supported concerns people killed at a political sit-in; article 833 in this same corpus cites the 'دون دينه' form. Whether the summary has quoted the wrong limb of a report the Sheikh gave in full can only be settled from the PDF.
'أغشت' is the Maghrebi month name for August, used alongside 'أغسطس' elsewhere in the same corpus. Not an error; noted so that a reviewer does not treat it as one.

translator_notes: A news summary of a signed fatwā whose text is behind two PDF downloads; marked source_is_excerpt_only and critical_for_display. The second signatory, Shaykh Muhammad Abd al-Rahman Ould Ahmad ('Ould Fata'), also appears in article 824. 'الشرع الحنيف' rendered 'the upright Sharia' — ḥanīf carries the sense of the primordial upright religion, not merely 'true'. CMS date is a bulk-upload timestamp, not a composition date.
dec: Names a sitting head of state as the executor of a conspiracy against Islam.
